headline: SPACE INVADERS rebuilt to its 1978 rules — and now it actually ends
lede: Batch 13 of the seed rollout turned out to be a fidelity rescue: the arcade's Invaders had no game-over at all. Three lives, respawn grace, an invasion landing that ends the run — rebuilt, seeded, replayable, live.

notes.text: The audit found worse than a missing seed: player death, a landing, even a cleared wave all silently restarted the game, and score was never incremented. Reporting done on that engine would have been a fake terminal — so the batch restored the original's rules first, then wired the seed contract on top.

Row bands score 30/20/20/10, the mystery UFO banks 50/100/150/300, three lives with the original's hold-and-blink respawn, and a landing ends the run even with lives in reserve. Waves rebuild faster and lower. Zero Math.random in the sim — ?seed=N replays the exact invasion.

The previous session died one PR short of shipping: its three pushed commits sat as a decodable corpse, the checkpoint-on-death law did its job, and this session resumed and merged them after re-running every gate. Two wardens also crossed wires assigning issues to occupied slots — both lanes yielded honestly, zero duplicated work.
The seed-pin floor rises to 44 titles, and a QA polish pass (#1495) is filed with the destructible bunkers flagged as the next fidelity milestone.
